extracted.intended_audience: trademark office examiners, trademark search professionals, intellectual property attorneys and other practitioners responsible for classifying figurative elements of marks
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Vienna Classification (CFE) to code and index the figurative elements of trademarks to facilitate anticipation searches and international exchange of trademark documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — facilitate anticipation searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Classification is essentially the practical one of facilitating trademark anticipation searches and obviating substantial reclassification work when documents are exchanged at the international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Classification to make anticipation searching effective; classification is administrative and does not determine the extent of legal protection afforded to a mark (Article 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — subject to each country's attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements prescribed by the Vienna Agreement, the scope of the Classification is that attributed to it by each country party to the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries may give the Classification legal scope beyond administrative use; they may apply it as principal or subsidiary system and may continue national classifications concurrently (transitional or permanent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical structure (categories, divisions, sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification constitutes a hierarchical system dividing figurative elements into categories, divisions and sections, proceeding from the general to the particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Table of Categories for rapid guidance, the Table of Categories and Divisions with Explanatory Notes to confine subject matter to a division, and the List of Categories, Divisions and Sections with Explanatory Notes to decide final placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding system — three-number notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every figurative element in a section is referred to by three numbers: the first (1–29) denotes the category, the second (1–19) the division, and the third (1–26) the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: representation of 'a little girl eating' belongs to Category 2, Division 5, Main Section 3 and Auxiliary Section 18; notation examples and format rules are given in Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary sections and main sections — marking and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are of two kinds: main sections and auxiliary sections. Auxiliary sections are intended for figurative elements already covered by main sections but grouped for ease of searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections have codes preceded by an 'A' in the Classification, are placed at the end of a division, and are not mandatory (national offices may use them at their discretion). Principal sections are marked with an asterisk in this edition's presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacant numbers for future expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the divisions and sections, certain numbers have been left vacant to permit the introduction of new divisions or sections when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume contiguous numbering; allow for future amendments and additions in workflows and databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of classification numbers in official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent offices of countries party to the Vienna Agreement are obliged to include in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks the numbers of the categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements have been placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Official documents and publications’ include trademark registers, registration and renewal certificates and office journals or gazettes; countries may, on accession, declare they do not undertake to include numbers of all or some sections (Article 4(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preceding label for classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers of categories, divisions and sections appearing in official documents should be preceded by the full name 'Classification of Figurative Elements' or by the abbreviation CFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee of Experts determined the abbreviation to be CFE; include edition indicator (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: The edition of the Vienna Classification according to which figurative elements are classified should be indicated by an Arabic numeral in round brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CFE (5) to indicate the fifth edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and formatting recommendations for CFE numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers of the category and division, and of the division and section should be separated by a point; numbers of two different sections by a comma; a dash indicates an uninterrupted range of sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: CFE 3.9.10,24,25; CFE 3.9.16-18; if section numbers are not included, use CFE 3.9. If several category/division classifications are necessary for one registration, indicate each separately in numerical order and separate them by a semicolon (e.g., CFE 1.1.2,10,25; 1.15.17; 2.9.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two essential operations for effective searching
rubrics_metrics.description: For anticipation searching to be effective two operations must first be completed: (i) consistent and correct classification (coding) of the figurative elements that will constitute the search file, and (ii) correct definition of the sections in which the prior marks have to be searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are interdependent; misclassification or incorrect selection of search sections undermines search effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence requirement for classifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for classification and for defining search sections must be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such persons should be able to assess figurative elements according to their distinguishing properties and take future needs of anticipation searching into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to follow Explanatory Notes and references
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the Classification, the user should abide strictly by the Explanatory Notes and the references given in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before starting, users should familiarize themselves with the Preface, Recommendations of the Committee of Experts, and the General Notes; Explanatory Notes on a category apply to subordinate divisions/sections (see list headings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part presentation for decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification is reproduced under three headings to assist users: (1) Table of Categories; (2) Table of Categories and Divisions, with Explanatory Notes; (3) List of Categories, Divisions and Sections, with Explanatory Notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three successive parts to narrow from category to final section placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are informative only
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples of figurative elements included in the publication are for information purposes only and are not an integral part of the Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat illustrative examples as normative definitions for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language authenticity and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification has been established in English and French, both texts being equally authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau may, in consultation with interested Governments and subject to Assembly decisions, establish official texts in other languages; translations should be treated in light of authenticity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts — roles and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts (one representative per country of the Special Union) is charged with making amendments and additions, addressing recommendations to facilitate use and promote uniform application, and taking measures to assist developing countries without financial implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee may invite observers, establish subcommittees/working groups, adopt rules of procedure, and requires specified majorities for different types of decisions (simple majority for general decisions; three-fourths for changes regarded as modifying basic structure or entailing substantial reclassification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal and notification timelines for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendments or additions may be made by competent Offices, the International Bureau, intergovernmental organizations represented in the Committee, or specially invited entities; such proposals shall be communicated to the International Bureau and submitted to members at least two months before the Committee session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions adopting amendments/additions are notified by the International Bureau and the amendments enter into force six months after dispatch of notifications; the International Bureau incorporates amendments which have entered into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: National discretion on inclusion of section numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries party to the Vienna Agreement may declare that they reserve the right not to include the numbers of all or some of the sections in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This declaration can be made at signature or at deposit of ratification/accession; auxiliary sections are in any event not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use when registration is entrusted to intergovernmental authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a country entrusts registration of marks to an intergovernmental authority, it shall take all possible measures to ensure that that authority uses the Classification in accordance with the Vienna Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States remain responsible for ensuring compliance with Agreement obligations where they delegate registration functions.
